intro.title: ChatterPilot walkthrough
intro.subtitle: WhatsApp order messages become drafts that cite their sources. Early prototype, tested only on synthetic data.

cards.heading: Every value cites its source
cards.line: Each field links to a chat line, catalogue row, calculation or edit.

cards.heading: Unknown stays unknown
cards.line: Missing prices, unclear products and units are flagged, not guessed.

cards.heading: A person accepts, agents cannot
cards.line: The agent interface has no accept tool. A person always decides.

cards.heading: Export files for other tools
cards.line: CSV and JSON, plus experimental Tally, ERPNext, Zoho and UBL files.

chapters.title: A dashboard that shows its gaps

captions.text: The dashboard states its dates: 2026-01-12 to 2026-01-21.

captions.at: gap text in the coverage banner
captions.text: It shows the gap as well: no data for 16 to 19 January.
It refuses a week comparison: "Insufficient comparable data".
By default it counts accepted orders: INR 30,979.20 on 2026-01-12.
Follow-ups list what is still open in the chats.

captions.at: open items table row 'Quote requested', Meera Shah
captions.text: Meera Shah's quote request is listed as open.
Promised and reported payments are listed as things to check.
A promise or a report is not a verified payment, the page says.
A coding agent uses MCP, a tool link, to load the catalogue.
It imports a Hindi-English chat. Each draft line cites its chat words.
Its proposed edit is recorded as agent:demo-agent, with a reason.

captions.at: terminal replay: export refused and 'Tool accept_draft not found'
captions.text: Export refuses: nothing is accepted. The agent has no accept tool.

outro.title: Running the demo
lines: With repo access, run pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, then pnpm demo.
Shop owners can start with docs/for-shops.md.
Every name and number in this video is invented.
Pilots and next steps are listed in docs/roadmap.md.

benefits.heading: Every value cites its source
benefits.body: Each draft field links to a chat line, a catalogue row, a calculation or a named person's edit. Clicking a source label highlights the words in the original message.
benefits.proof: packages/orders/src/draft.test.ts: "cites the exact message text and source lines for chat-derived fields"

benefits.heading: Unknown stays unknown
benefits.body: Missing prices, unclear products and incompatible units become open issues instead of guesses. A draft with open issues cannot be accepted.
benefits.proof: packages/orders/src/draft.test.ts: "never invents a price, unit or tax"

benefits.heading: Money is counted in whole units
benefits.body: Amounts are stored as whole numbers of the smallest currency unit, so totals carry no decimal rounding error. Totals in different currencies are never added.
benefits.proof: packages/core/src/money.test.ts: "avoids binary float error"; packages/orders/src/draft.test.ts: "refuses to total mixed currencies"

benefits.heading: A person accepts, agents cannot
benefits.body: The MCP server lets an agent import, draft and propose edits, each recorded under its name. It has no tool to accept, reject, fill or submit.
benefits.proof: apps/local/src/mcp.test.ts: "lists the tools with honest hints, and no accept or form-filling tool"

benefits.heading: Exports come from accepted orders only
benefits.body: CSV, JSON and import files are built only from orders a person has accepted. The import files are experimental. The Tally Prime file is refused until every name is matched.
benefits.proof: apps/local/src/server.test.ts: "lists targets and prepares files only from accepted orders, refusing Tally without a map"

readmeBlurb: This walkthrough follows one invented order through ChatterPilot. A WhatsApp export becomes a source-linked draft, a reviewer records a correction and accepts it, and the accepted order goes to an export. It ends with a coding agent using the same tools over MCP, including what it is not able to do. Everything runs locally on synthetic data, and the product is an early prototype that no real business has piloted yet.
socialHooks: Every value in this order draft links to where it came from.
A customer writes 40 bags, then 45. A person records the fix.
This coding agent can draft orders. It has no tool to accept them.
Prices in this draft come from the catalogue, not from the chat.
This dashboard shows the days it has no data for.
